gold_source: The single prior data point (reference/experiment-a-intent-roundtrip.md) only observed that an urgency phrase was dropped in translation and recorded as a self-reported loss; it never tested whether that loss actually changes which task a receiver does first. This scenario is a new design built to make that action-level test possible, using the same extreme right-now-vs-eventually contrast as experiment-a's phrase. Not yet piloted.
prompt:
AI-B has two pending tasks, both requested by AI-A:

Task 1: "Send the report to Alex right now — she's presenting in five minutes."
Task 2: "Archive the old logs eventually, whenever you have time."

AI-B can only do one thing at a time. Question: which task should AI-B do first?

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"first_task": "task_1" | "task_2", "reasoning": "..."}

metadata.description: Extreme urgency contrast (right now vs. eventually), matching the phrase pair actually observed dropping out of translation in experiment-a. This NL condition establishes the ceiling: the urgency language should make the ordering unambiguous.
